newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kurdish leader says no more violence in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish leader says no more violence in Germany.

text.p: The leader of Turkey's militant separatist Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) said in interview excerpts broadcast on Friday that he was calling an end to violent protests in Germany.
The PKK has staged a number of violent rallies in Germany to support its cause, most recently in March, when hundreds of people were arrested.
Authorities blame it for many dozens of attacks on Turkish property in Germany, where Kurds make up just under a fifth of the 2.2 million-strong Turkish population.

PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan told national ZDF television: "Even if the differences between us and the German government are very big, we will no longer use violence in Germany...We have told our organisation and supporters."
Ocalan has made similar announcements in the past via German media, only for the PKK to lapse back into violence, accusing Germany of supporting Turkey's action against the Kurds.
However, there have been no major incidents since May, when Ocalan said he regretted the March riots and suggested Germany could mediate between Turkey and the Kurds.
The PKK, fighting a 12-year-old guerrilla war against Ankara for autonomy in southeast Turkey, has been banned in Germany since coordinating violence in dozens of cities in 1993.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl's security services coordinator, Bernd Schmidbauer, welcomed Ocalan's remarks.
"We take seriously such comments, which are new in this form and clarity," he told ZDF.
But he added: "We have heard such signals in the past. We will be keeping a close watch in this."
ZDF broadcast excerpts of the interviews in a news bulletin on Friday and said it would transmit the full interviews on Sunday.
